items.stem: Bea is 5 times as old as her niece. In 16 years, Bea will be three times as old as the niece. How old is Bea now?

reveal.terms: "5 times as old" means the age is the younger person's age multiplied by 5.
reveal.shortcut: Try the choices. If Bea is 80, the niece is 16. In 16 years: 96 and 32. 96 = 3 × 32, so it works.
reveal.why_correct: 80 is right. Algebra: niece = s, Bea = 5s; 5s + 16 = 3(s + 16) gives s = 16, so Bea = 80.

why_wrong.o1: 96 is Bea's age 16 years from now, not today.
why_wrong.o2: 16 is the niece's age now, not Bea's.
why_wrong.o3: 32 is the niece's age 16 years from now.

items.stem: How many consecutive terms may a Member of the House of Representatives serve?

items.stem: Under Art. II, Sec. 28, the State adopts and implements a policy of full public disclosure of what?

items.stem: How often may impeachment proceedings be initiated against the same official?

options.text: Not more than twice a year
Not more than once within a period of one year

reveal.terms: This item is about the 1987 Constitution, Art. XI, Sec. 3(5).
